english.title: Possess potentially dangerous item on the Tyne and Wear Metro
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..), without written permission of the Operator or an authorised person

(A)_[brought an item, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ITEM..), onto]_
(B)_[allowed an item, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ITEM..), to remain on]_

the Tyne and Wear Metro at **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..) which, in the opinion of an authorised person may have threatened, annoyed, soiled or damaged a person or property
english.legislation: Contrary to byelaws 2(1) and 31(1) of the Tyne and Wear Metro Byelaws made under sections 58 and 62 of the Tyneside Metropolitan Railway Act 1973.

english.notes:
(i) Byelaw 2(1) provides that "potentially dangerous items" will include:- (i) a loaded weapon of any kind; (ii) any inflammable, explosive or corrosive substance and (iii) any item which is or may become dangerous.
(i) Byelaw 30 make provisions in relation to name and addresses.
(ii) Byelaw 31(2) provides powers for the removal of persons.
(iii) When using these powers, anauthorised person, including a constable, must show his/her identification if requested.
(iv) Byelaw 31(6) provides that an authorised person acting in the course of his duties shall not be liable for breach of byelaw 2.
(v) Byelaw 2(3) provides that if any person in charge of an item in breach of Byelaw 2 is asked by an authorised person to remove it and fails to do so immediately it may be removed by or under the direction of an authorised person.
